newsitem.title: USA: Republican extends lead in close Ore. Senate race.
newsitem.headline: Republican extends lead in close Ore. Senate race.

text.p: Republican Gordon Smith inched ahead Thursday in the nation's final undecided Senate race, but stopped short of declaring victory with more than 400,000 absentee ballots yet to be counted.

According to the latest unofficial returns, Smith, Oregon's state Senate president, led Democratic businessman Tom Bruggere 49 to 46 percent with a gap of nearly 20,000 votes out of more than 700,000 counted so far.
By law county officials had until Friday at midnight to finish counting, and several indicated they would be working up to the deadline.

All three major local television stations in Portland declared Smith the winner. The candidate, who narrowly lost to Democrat Ron Wyden in a race for the state's other Senate seat this year, expressed confidence the results would hold.
But an official with the Bruggere campaign pointed out that more than 100,000 ballots had yet to be counted in Multnomah County alone, where the Democrat was winning 62 percent of the votes.
"By the end of the day tomorrow we'll know who the winner is," said Lauren Moughon, Bruggere's communications director. "Until then we'll take a wait-and-see attitude."
Even with the Oregon race undecided Republicans already have increased their Senate majority by at least one vote, to 54-45 from the current 53-47.
